title: Paired Associative Stimulation of the Motor Cortex and the Dorsal Roots of the Cervical Spine for the Recovery of Arm and Hand Function in Chronic Middle Cerebral Artery Stroke. ASCLEPIUS Safety Evaluation Pilot Study
official: Paired Associative Stimulation of the Motor Cortex and the Dorsal Roots of the Cervical Spine for the Recovery of Arm and Hand Function in Chronic Middle Cerebral Artery Stroke. ASCLEPIUS Safety Evaluation Pilot Study (Epidural Associative Stimulation of the Cerebral Cortex and Spinal Cord to Increase Plasticity in Upper Limb Stroke)
summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to learn whether paired associative stimulation (PAS) of the primary motor cortex and the cervical spinal dorsal roots, delivered through implanted epidural electrodes and combined with neurorehabilitation, is safe in adults with chronic paresis or paralysis of the arm and hand after a stroke in the territory of the middle cerebral artery.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\* What adverse events occur during 12 months of follow-up with this treatment?

Secondary questions are whether the stimulation is feasible (whether pairing the corresponding electrode contacts of the motor cortex and the cervical spinal cord increases the motor response to stimulation) and whether it shows preliminary signs of efficacy on upper limb motor function, quality of life and caregiver burden.

Researchers will compare PAS plus rehabilitation with sham stimulation plus rehabilitation during a two-month double-blind phase.

Participants will:

* Have epidural electrodes surgically implanted over the primary motor cortex and the cervical spinal cord, connected to an implanted pulse generator
* Receive PAS or sham stimulation together with rehabilitation sessions for two months
* If assigned to sham stimulation, receive open-label PAS plus rehabilitation for a further two months
* Attend follow-up visits for 12 months

interventions.name: Epidural paired associative stimulation of the motor cortex and cervical dorsal roots

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Older than 18 and younger than 85 years of age.
* Single ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke with more than 6 months of evolution, with involvement of the hand and arm, that has shown no improvement with standard treatment after two previous reviews.
* No intercurrent strokes.
* Moderate functional impairment on the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE score 20 to 49).
* Good trunk control.
* Meets the safety requirements for imaging studies.
* Cooperative.
* Signed informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Severe disease or disorder (e.g., cancer, severe cardiac or respiratory disease, renal failure) or cognitive impairment (MoCA \< 24), visual impairment or language impairment that could affect the ability to participate in a rehabilitation program.
* Presence of any previously implanted medical device.
* Severe claustrophobia.
* Major depression or any emotional disorder with a severe deficit of attention or cooperation that could cause difficulty in hand function.
* Modified Ashworth Scale score of 3 or higher.

Withdrawal criterion after enrollment: absence of evidence of partial preservation of the affected corticospinal tract on MRI tractography or neurophysiological testing (motor evoked potentials by transcranial magnetic stimulation).
